papers.title: [Editorial] Rethinking threats to human survival
papers.summary: Much health advocacy is driven by single-issue activism. Communities with a common interest—from AIDS to child health, climate to tobacco control—focus intensely on their own domain. And understandably so. Important progress has been made through often courageous direct action. But this sharply competitive approach is, according to a new Lancet Commission on 21st Century Global Threats to Health, dangerously flawed. Indeed, perhaps the most important contribution of this Commission is to move global health beyond the consideration of individual harms.

papers.title: [Comment] Establishing cardiovascular safety of the small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist orforglipron in type 2 diabetes
papers.summary: Cardiovascular outcomes trials with GLP-1 receptor agonists, which to date have largely comprised peptide analogues of the incretin hormone GLP-1, have evolved from studies primarily designed to establish cardiovascular safety to trials demonstrating cardiovascular benefit.1–3 Substantial reductions in major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and kidney protection have been demonstrated with multiple GLP-1 receptor agonists for subcutaneous administration,1–3 and, more recently, with oral semaglutide.

papers.title: [Comment] Making every vial count: fractional dosing of yellow fever vaccine
papers.summary: Yellow fever is an important public health problem, but vaccine manufacturing cannot be scaled up easily, making it necessary to use existing vaccine stocks to protect as many people as possible. Fractional doses, usually one-fifth of a vial, have been used during outbreaks. The use of fractional doses is supported by evidence in adults showing immunogenicity1,2 and is endorsed by WHO.3 Yellow fever vaccine is routinely given to infants and young children in endemic areas, but whether fractional dosing is effective in children was unclear until recent trials from 2023 and 2026 addressed this question.

papers.title: [Comment] A novel and effective treatment for fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva
papers.summary: Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP) is among the most devastating musculoskeletal disorders. FOP is caused by activating variants in ACVR1, most often arising de novo, and is characterised by congenital malformations of the great toes, followed by episodic flare-ups and progressive heterotopic ossification in soft tissues.1,2 Lesions can be triggered by minor trauma, intramuscular injections, or surgery, but can also arise without an identifiable trigger. Over time, heterotopic bone forms a second skeleton, progressively restricting movement of the jaw, spine, hips, shoulders, and thorax.

papers.title: [Comment] Shortening treatment to accelerate hepatitis C elimination
papers.summary: Simple oral direct-acting antiviral treatment for hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection has transformed clinical management and paved the way for elimination.1 The first pan-genotypic fixed-dose combination regimen, sofosbuvir–velpatasvir, was approved for use in 2016, with the second, glecaprevir–pibrentasvir, following in 2017. Both recommended first-line HCV treatments for people with or without compensated cirrhosis share several important features—high efficacy, excellent tolerability, oral administration, once daily dosing—but differ by pill burden, treatment duration, and availability, with sofosbuvir–velpatasvir prescribed for 12 weeks (one tablet daily; available as a generic formulation) and glecaprevir–pibrentasvir for 8 weeks (three tablets daily; under patent protection).

papers.title: [Comment] 21st century global threats to health are not what you think

papers.title: [Comment] Offline: In praise of astrologers, sorcerers, and magicians

That fight intensified this week with the publication of our Commission on 21st century global threats to health. Commissioners reviewed almost 400 risks to human health. They identified two existential threats and 15 major catastrophic threats. The peer review process was instructive about how these findings might be received.

papers.title: [Perspectives] John Wong: making an impact on population health at scale

The problem is that we haven’t allowed people to get to an older age healthy”, says John Wong, Executive Director of the Centre for Population Health at the National University of Singapore (NUS) and Executive Director of The Yong Pung How and Yong Wei-Woo Centre at the National University Health System (NUHS), Singapore. “Two-thirds of the world is now below the fertility replacement rate, and unless we keep our populations healthy throughout their whole lifespan, we’ll have this major challenge of more and more unwell older people”, continued Wong, who is also Isabel Chan Professor in Medical Sciences in the Division of Haematology-Oncology at the Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine, NUS, and Emeritus Consultant in the Department of Haematology-Oncology, National University Cancer Institute, NUHS, Singapore.

papers.title: [Perspectives] Shadows and interiority

This is the absolute opposite of what author Chloe Aridjis does in The Shadow of the Object.

papers.title: [Perspectives] Beyond the battlefield: war and global health security

Monitoring groups documented over 600 attacks on health care, resulting in the deaths of hundreds of health-care workers throughout the conflict. Hospitals in eastern Aleppo and other contested regions were reduced to rubble. Surgeons operated in underground rooms illuminated by generators, and ambulances were targeted while transporting patients between sites.

papers.title: [Perspectives] Temporal rationing: a man with gastric cancer in Colombia

In 2010, he presented to a general practitioner with several months of abdominal heaviness and non-exertional substernal burning. The physician provisionally diagnosed gastro-oesophageal reflux disease and prescribed omeprazole. However, Pepe's symptoms slowly worsened and 10 weeks later he returned to the physician, who ordered a gastroscopy, which occurred 2 months later, revealing an ulcerated mass.

papers.title: [Correspondence] WHO should adjust its cervical cancer plan – Authors’ reply

This point was highlighted by Brisson and colleagues1 and in an accompanying Comment2 that warned that human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination implementation must not follow the same inequitable path.

Their supporting self-citation was in press, whereas Borland and colleagues,2 also referenced in the Comment, rely on Mendelsohn and colleagues3 for their New Zealand evidence, which stops at 2022–23.

papers.title: [Correspondence] Smoking rates: when should harm-reduction evidence be updated? – Authors’ reply
papers.summary: The striking feature of recent New Zealand smoking trends is the statistically significant acceleration in smoking decline after 2019, not the subsequent plateau. The critical issue is why smoking declined so rapidly after vaping became widespread.

papers.title: [Correspondence] Underuse of neuromodulation in depression care – Authors’ reply

Furthermore, in our view, some of these interventions should in fact be used much less, if at all. However, before turning to these points, it is necessary to set a few matters straight.

papers.title: [Correspondence] Cultural calibration is needed in global mental disorder burden estimates – Authors’ reply
papers.summary: We thank Yasuhiro Kotera for commenting on our Article reporting the global prevalence and burden of mental disorders from the Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study (GBD) 2023.1 We welcome their emphasis on the importance of cultural comparability when interpreting GBD findings. In the GBD study, we have an obligation to provide the best available burden estimates for mental disorders across all locations included. We work on the principle that uncertain burden estimates, despite limitations to the underlying data or analytical process, are preferable to no estimate for a condition or population.

papers.title: [Correspondence] Optimising standard of care in non-small-cell lung cancer trials

papers.title: [Correspondence] Optimising standard of care in non-small-cell lung cancer trials – Authors’ reply

papers.title: [The Lancet Commissions] The Lancet Commission on 21st century global threats to health
papers.summary: This report from the Lancet Commission on 21st century global threats to health lays out a foresight-driven, health-focused approach to identifying and prioritising major threats to global health over the remainder of the century. We argue that recent global shocks (including COVID-19, Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease, major geopolitical conflict, accelerating climate impacts, rapid shifts in development assistance, and the emergence of powerful artificial intelligence [AI] systems) show how quickly assumptions about stability can be overturned—and why governments and multilateral institutions must counter short-termism and localism with systematic, repeatable risk assessment and preparedness planning.

papers.title: [Review] Addressing threats to future global health—what is the right timeframe?
papers.summary: Our decisions today can support or threaten future human health. Insofar as we protect the planet or invest in fruitful research on pandemic countermeasures, we promote future wellbeing and health, sometimes at the present generation's expense. As we warm the planet, accelerate antibiotic resistance, or consume finite natural resources, we might serve present-day wellbeing or health at the expense of future generations. To decide which such trade-offs are legitimate or advisable, we need to know how to balance the health interests of future generations against each other and against our own.

papers.title: [Editorial] Counteracting the rise of antimicrobial resistance in Shigella

Shigellosis is one of the leading causes of global diarrhoeal disease deaths, especially in children younger than 5 years. Shigella disproportionately affects low-income and middle-income countries (LMICs), where transmission occurs mainly through the oral–faecal route due to poor water, sanitation, and hygiene practices. Shigella is divided into four main species: S dysenteriae, S boydii, S flexneri, and S sonnei, of which all have multiple serotypes except S flexneri.

papers.summary: A cohort study in France assessed the monoclonal antibody nirsevimab against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in infants at 1 year and 2 years after immunisation. Outcomes were examined in infants born before the first RSVpreF vaccination campaign for pregnant women started in September 2024. Nirsevimab was associated with lower rates of RSV-lower respiratory tract-related hospitalisations during the first year after immunisation: 299 (0·8%) of 37 366 immunised versus 899 (2·4%) of 37 366 non-immunised infants in 2023, and 456 (0·5%) of 87 763 immunised versus 1711 (1.9%) of 87 763 non-immunised infants in 2024 (weighted hazard ratios 0·34, 95% CI 0·30–0·39 for the 2023 cohort and 0·28, 0.25–0·31 for the 2024 cohort, corresponding to nirsevimab effectiveness estimates of 66% and 72%, respectively).

papers.title: [Obituary] Bruce Ribner
papers.summary: Pioneering infectious disease physician and epidemiologist died on July 19, 2026, aged 80 years.

papers.title: [Profile] Mahboubeh Hajiabdolbaghi—advancing ID care in Iran
papers.summary: Mahboubeh Hajiabdolbaghi was born and raised in Tehran, where her parents encouraged education, curiosity, and independence. She studied medicine at Tehran University of Medical Sciences (TUMS), at a time when only around one in ten medical students was female. “The passion for learning my mother and father gave me has stayed with me throughout my life”, she tells The Lancet Infectious Diseases. She retired as Professor of Infectious Diseases at TUMS in 2022 and but continues in clinical practice in Tehran.

papers.title: [Clinical Picture] Lymphoma-like endoscopic appearance of lymphogranuloma venereum
papers.summary: A 34-year-old man with HIV who had sex with men was referred to our hospital after experiencing bloody mucoid stools for 6 months. He had initially presented to a local clinic, where haemorrhoids were suspected and topical treatment was prescribed. However, because his symptoms persisted, he was referred for further investigation. Colonoscopy revealed a circumferential 50 mm volcano-like rectal ulcer with an irregular, thick heaped-up margin and a deep ulcer base (figure A), accompanied by a smaller shallow round ulcer.

papers.title: Multi-omics atlas of chronic exercise
papers.summary: A 22-tissue multi-omics atlas of chronic exercise is generated, detailing tissue-, sex-, and time-dependent molecular adaptations and cell-type-specific epigenetic remodeling in skeletal muscle. The atlas reveals coordinated transcriptomic, epigenetic, proteomic, and metabolic remodeling across the body.

papers.title: Functional diversification of the cephalopod proteome by RNA editing
papers.summary: Coleoid cephalopods edit their RNA at a level far beyond other animals, but the functional consequences to the proteome have been largely unknown. Proteomic detection of recoded sites reveals that single amino acid edits alter protein stability, subcellular localization, post-translational modification, and organelle function.

papers.title: An opioid efficacy switch for reversible optical control of analgesia
papers.summary: Azo-morphine-3 (AM-3) is a photoswitchable ligand that toggles between low and high efficacy states to control mu-opioid receptor activity in vitro and in vivo both in the brain and periphery. AM-3 provides a powerful tool to probe the structural basis of opioid efficacy and enables spatiotemporally precise control of analgesia across pain models with reduced side effects compared with systemic drugs.

papers.title: Cellular self-organization orchestrates ferroptosis propagation
papers.summary: Local cell-cell interactions give rise to emergent cellular patterns that encode ferroptosis-sensitive and -resistant fates and establish polarized lipid organization within cells. These coupled biochemical and biophysical properties enable self-organized cell populations to orient and confine otherwise isotropic, unbounded ferroptosis propagation, revealing a systems-level mechanism that regulates collective cell fate.

papers.title: Mitochondria-targeted tetraoxanes initiate lipid peroxidation to drive ferroptosis and tumor suppression
papers.summary: Pan et al. report tetraoxane-containing compounds WMK-1/2 as first-generation mitochondrial lipid peroxidation inducers that bypass GPX4- and retinol-mediated defenses to trigger a distinct “mito-ferroptosis” sub-pathway, demonstrating potent bioavailable tumor-suppressive activity across multiple in vivo models.

papers.title: A phenome-wide structural variant map from 467,152 UK Biobank genomes
papers.summary: By studying nearly half a million human genomes, this work shows that structural variants, large changes in DNA sequence greater than 50 base pairs, are an important and previously underrecognized source of human disease risk. The resulting resource reveals rare and regulatory structural variants linked to disease, providing insights into human biology and accelerating the development of medicines.

papers.title: Sensing endoplasmic reticulum redox state by ethylene receptors
A pseudoenzyme sensor of trehalose-6-phosphate directly represses the metabolic integrator SnRK1 in plants
papers.summary: In Arabidopsis, pseudoenzyme class II T6P synthase functions as a T6P sensor that directly represses the master metabolic regulator SnRK1, highlighting a conserved switch that couples carbon availability to metabolic homeostasis in plants.

papers.title: A high-dimensional population code in the bat motor cortex during natural dexterous flight
papers.summary: Bats use their hand-like wings to reproduce natural flights with wingbeat-level precision. Rather than mainly tracking the wingbeat cycle, the wing motor cortex generates sparse, distinct population states with little shared variance across wingbeats, resulting in a high-dimensional code distinct from that typically observed in constrained tasks.

papers.title: Mechanisms of transcription control by distal enhancers from single-gene nanoscopy
papers.summary: High-resolution real-time imaging of enhancer-promoter communication reveals how the two genomic loci are actively brought together through cohesin-mediated loop extrusion and how E-P interactions are temporally coordinated with transcriptional bursts. Unexpectedly, components of the RNA Pol II general machinery form nanoscale clusters at distal enhancers, and embedding the promoter into such clusters boosts GTF activities and triggers burst initiation.

papers.title: PTPRS mediates invasion of tetanus neurotoxin into the central nervous system
papers.summary: Tetanus neurotoxin enters the central nervous system through motor neurons. This study identifies PTPRS as the long-sought retrograde transport receptor that directs toxin trafficking in motor neurons into the spinal cord, uncovering a host pathway that can be targeted for post-exposure treatment and for drug delivery into the central nervous system.

papers.title: Rare k-mers reveal centromere haplogroups underlying human diversity and cancer translocations
papers.summary: By defining centromere haplogroups from rare k-mer variation, Shiraishi et al. uncover extensive hidden diversity and link centromere structure to human evolution and disease-associated genomic instability.

papers.title: Mapping transcriptional responses to cellular perturbations with RNA fingerprinting
papers.summary: RNA fingerprinting is a statistical framework that infers causal regulators from single-cell experiments by mapping their transcriptional responses onto reference perturbation dictionaries.

papers.title: A fluctuation test for gastruloid heterogeneity
papers.summary: Organoids grown side by side under identical conditions vary unpredictably, a longstanding obstacle to their use. Adapting the logic of a classic fluctuation test to gastruloids grown from single stem cells shows that this variability is largely inherited rather than induced and is traceable to fluctuations in the state of the founding cell.

papers.title: Comprehensive lineage tracing maps the landscape of cell fate decisions in mouse embryogenesis
papers.summary: We use PEtracer to reconstruct high-resolution lineage histories for >1.4 million cells from E7.5 to E10.0 during mouse development, providing a quantitative view of fate bias, restriction timing, and clonal output. Across diverse tissues, these data reveal highly reproducible lineage architectures and define general and tissue-specific strategies of cell fate specification.

papers.title: A non-canonical function of glutathione to suppress ferroptosis via FSP1
papers.summary: Glutathione (GSH) robustly defends against ferroptosis independently of GPX4. FSP1 utilizes GSH to reduce ubiquinone and subsequently inhibits ferroptosis, which is distinct from the NAD(P)H-FAD axis. Targeting the FSP1-GSH axis efficiently alleviated ferroptosis-induced tissue injury.

papers.title: A spatiotemporal lifecycle atlas decodes spatial coordination in rice
papers.summary: A 3D spatiotemporal cell atlas of rice spanning the entire seed-to-seed lifecycle. Developmental trajectories are captured, and the spatially distinct roles of OsARF1 in rice development and dorsoventral endosperm asymmetry related to starch and protein accumulation are revealed.

papers.title: SPARCS enables scalable recovery of complex image-based phenotypes for genetic screening
papers.summary: Current genetic screens face a trade-off between scaling to large mutant libraries and measuring information-rich phenotypes. SPARCS automates laser microdissection to enable pooled forward genetic screens for complex image-based phenotypes at scale. By physically recovering individual mutants, SPARCS supports multimodal profiling of hits beyond genotyping, including via mass spectrometry-based proteomics.

papers.title: Cancer competition for vitamin B2 creates metabolic checkpoint for T cell ferroptosis
papers.summary: A CRISPR screen of solute carriers reveals that T cells depend on SLC52A3 for VB2 uptake, whereas tumors preferentially exploit SLC52A2 to outcompete them, thereby driving T cell ferroptosis. Enforced SLC52A3 overexpression in T cells reverses this metabolic competition and enhances their antitumor activity.

papers.title: Global, site-resolved analysis of ubiquitylation occupancy and turnover rate reveals systems properties
Salicylic acid engages central metabolic regulators SnRK1 and TOR to govern immunity by differential phosphorylation of NPR1
papers.summary: The immune signal SA triggers metabolic changes to activate SnRK1 while inhibiting TOR. These central metabolic kinases antagonistically phosphorylate the key immune regulator NPR1, thereby coupling cellular metabolic state to systemic acquired resistance.

papers.title: Gut microbiota primes stroke severity via the AHR in intestinal dendritic cells
papers.summary: Indole-producing Escherichia coli worsens ischemic stroke through the activation of aryl hydrocarbon receptor signaling in dendritic cells. Limiting AHR signaling in DCs promotes gut-derived DC migration to the meninges, expands meningeal regulatory T cells, and reduces neuroinflammation. This microbiota-AHR axis offers a promising therapeutic target.

papers.title: Spatial evolution of a cachexia-promoting microenvironment in pancreatic cancer
papers.summary: Pancreatic cancer cachexia is accompanied by progressive assembly of a spatially organized tumor-macrophage-fibroblast niche. Reciprocal signaling among the cellular populations in the niche is associated with muscle wasting and cachexia progression.

papers.title: Microbiome signatures linked to cancer and treatment adverse events in a real-world cohort
papers.summary: In a large, real-world mixed-cancer cohort, analyses accounting for comorbidities and additional confounders indicate that most microbiome alterations are shared across cancers rather than specific to individual cancers. Distinct associations are limited to a subset of cancers and, in separate analyses, to age of onset and specific treatment-related adverse events.

papers.title: Cargo crosslinking nucleates AP-1 lattice formation
papers.summary: Cargo has traditionally been viewed as a passive substrate of coat-mediated transport. Cryo-EM reveals that cargo containing tandem sorting motifs directly promotes higher-order adaptor assembly by bridging AP-1 complexes, enabling efficient trafficking and neuronal development in zebrafish.

papers.title: Non-invasive control of gene editing in vivo by photoswitchable Cas12f and focused ultrasound
papers.summary: Remote activation of a single-AAV-deliverable photoswitchable Cas12f system enables precise spatial and temporal control of genome editing in deep tissues without surgery or implanted devices.

papers.title: Opposing functions of gut immunomodulatory metabolites on CAR-T therapy
papers.summary: Gut microbial taxonomy alone is a poor predictor of CAR-T cell therapy outcome. Instead, specific gut immunomodulatory metabolites exert opposing effects on CAR-T cell function and tumor control, identifying microbial metabolism as a potential target to predict and improve CAR-T cell outcomes.

papers.title: In-cell discovery and characterization of a non-canonical bacterial protein translocation-folding complex
papers.summary: In-cell cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) combined with proteomics, integrative structural modeling, and bioinformatics enables discovery and functional annotation of uncharacterized proteins. In the minimal bacterium Mycoplasma pneumoniae, this reveals a complex that links Sec-based protein translocation and extracellular folding, capable of supporting both co- and post-translational pathways.

papers.title: Single-cell visual proteomics of a minimal bacterium reveals structural coordination of gene expression machineries
papers.summary: Cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) resolves and quantifies an almost complete view of bacterial translation, revealing how gene expression machineries coordinate across the processes of transcription, translation, and membrane engagement directly within a minimal bacterium.

papers.title: A pericyte-to-myofibroblast transition links APOE4 to cerebrovascular degeneration
papers.summary: APOE4 causes a pericyte-to-myofibroblast transition that promotes cerebrovascular fibrosis and perivascular amyloid accumulation. TGF-β inhibition reverses this pathological remodeling and thus presents a therapeutic strategy to restore cerebrovascular homeostasis in these high-risk individuals.

papers.title: Shifts in embryonic oxygen levels cue heterochrony in limb initiation
papers.summary: Mammalian embryos see a substantial increase in available oxygen once the placenta forms. This increase in oxygen exposure serves as a trigger for initiating the development of the hindlimb, thus controlling developmental timing and, more broadly, linking the maternal environment to evolutionary changes in body plan.

papers.title: Microbial signaling coordinates group oviposition and predator defense in migratory locusts
papers.summary: This study reveals an egg-associated bacterial signaling mechanism that couples reproductive synchronization with offspring defense in the locust L. migratoria, expanding the functional landscape of insect-microbe-predator interactions and demonstrating how microbial signals can shape complex ecological behaviors.

papers.title: Direct cell-to-cell transmission of retrotransposons
papers.summary: Retrotransposons can infect neighboring cells using a mechanism that relies on a small fusogen-like protein rather than on the envelope protein that is typically required for infection.

papers.title: Projection-defined modules reveal mouse motor cortex architecture
papers.summary: The mouse motor cortex divides into 16 spatially organized modules based on distinct subcortical projections. This specificity covaries with cortical connectivity patterns and cell-type composition along two spatial axes, thereby defining the rules by which motor cortex modules integrate with granularity into brainwide and precisely wired neuronal networks to influence movement.

papers.title: CD4 T cells convert transient responses to KRAS inhibition to durable remissions in pancreatic cancer
papers.summary: An AI-designed IL-21 mimetic converts transient KRAS inhibitor responses into durable pancreatic cancer remissions through CD4 T cells, independent of CD8 T cells and tumor MHC class I expression.

papers.title: Chloroplasts balance energy production and stress resilience via a cold-induced signaling pathway
papers.summary: Cold-stress signals are transmitted to chloroplasts and subsequently trigger cold responses through an RAF-like bi-kinase module where cytoplasmic RAF3 and plasma membrane RAF6 translocate to chloroplasts, where they inhibit photosynthetic activity but activate nuclear cold-responsive gene expression.

papers.title: mRNA-encoding CD19-targeting T cell engager for refractory immune thrombocytopenia
papers.summary: An mRNA-lipid nanoparticle-encoded CD19×CD3 T cell engager depletes B cells with attenuated cytokine release in preclinical models. In three patients with treatment-refractory immune thrombocytopenia, treatment with this T cell engager achieved sustained platelet recovery over 6 months, suggesting that mRNA-encoded T cell engagers represent a promising therapeutic approach for resetting autoreactive immunity in B cell-driven autoimmune disease.

papers.title: Akkermansia muciniphila attenuates macrophage efferocytosis to enhance anti-PD-1 efficacy in microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer
papers.summary: Jiang et al. show that Akkermansia muciniphila reshapes the tumor immune environment to overcome PD-1 resistance in microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer (MSS CRC). Mechanistic studies and a phase 1 trial support gut microbiome modulation as a promising strategy to improve immunotherapy in this common treatment-resistant disease.

papers.title: Gemella morbillorum promotes colorectal tumorigenesis through barrier disruption and invasion-dependent DNA damage
papers.summary: Meyers, Medina Evora, Molina Tijeras, et al. show that the colorectal cancer-associated oral bacterium Gemella morbillorum (Gm) promotes tumor progression. Colonization of the colon by Gm increases intestinal permeability, enables epithelial cell invasion, reshapes host lipid metabolism, and triggers DNA damage, collectively accelerating disease progression.

papers.title: Akkermansia muciniphila protects against endometritis through a tyrosol-mediated gut-uterus axis
papers.summary: Qu et al. show that the Akkermansia muciniphila (AKK) protects against endometritis by promoting production of the microbial metabolite tyrosol, which reaches the uterus and suppresses inflammation. These findings reveal a metabolite-mediated gut-uterus axis linking the intestinal microbiota to reproductive health.

papers.title: Native pathogen-phage networks reveal multilayered defense and gut-active anti-phage immunity
papers.summary: Wang et al. map >1,000 interactions between Salmonella isolates and bacteriophages to measure the relative contributions of surface features and intracellular defense to phage resistance across a major human pathogen. They further identify AppA, which blocks DNA packaging by targeting the large terminase and restricts phage replication within mammalian hosts.

papers.title: Myo-inositol metabolism counteracts mycotoxin hijacking and confers broad resistance to fungal diseases in crops
papers.summary: Xia et al. reveal that the Fusarium mycotoxin DON hijacks host central metabolism through NAD+-dependent enzymes to promote disease and identify MIPS as a key safeguard that redirects myo-inositol metabolism to drive PI(4,5)P2-dependent vacuolar sequestration of DON, maintaining metabolic homeostasis and conferring broad Fusarium resistance in crops.

papers.title: A commensal-derived sugar protects against obesity by regulating immunometabolism
papers.summary: Tan et al. identify a human commensal bacterium, Clostridium immunis—and its bioactive phosphocholine-modified exopolysaccharide (EPS)—that reduces visceral adiposity and weight gain in mice. By decreasing IL-22 levels, this EPS increases metabolic activity specifically in visceral fat. Metagenomic analyses suggest that this bacterial pathway may be conserved in humans.

papers.title: Embracing macrophage complexity for research and translation
papers.summary: Ginhoux, Mulder, Arcila-Barrera, and Amit argue that macrophage identity is best understood not as a set of discrete subsets or a binary M1/M2 axis but as combinations of modular gene programs. They propose an extensible, program-based classification of macrophage states and discuss how it reframes macrophage-directed therapy from targeting individual checkpoints toward program-level reprogramming.

papers.title: Lactate dehydrogenase A-dependent redox control of selective mRNA translation directs monocyte fate commitment
papers.summary: Metabolic reprogramming regulates immune cell function; however, how metabolic signals instruct early monocyte fate commitment remains unclear. Yang et al. show that LDHA-dependent cytosolic NAD+ regeneration promotes selective HIF1α translation, supporting commitment to a protective NOS2+ macrophage fate and revealing a broader link between redox metabolism and cell fate decisions.

papers.title: Dan Kastner (1951–2026)
papers.summary: Daniel L. Kastner, physician-scientist, geneticist, mentor, and scientific leader, transformed our understanding of human inflammatory disease. His death is a profound loss not only to the immunology community but also to the numerous patients and families whose illnesses he elucidated—and for whom, in many cases, he developed effective treatments. Called the “father of autoinflammatory diseases,” Dan did more than discover individual disorders: he defined an entirely new category of human disease.

papers.title: Skin-resident CXCR6+ memory CD4+ T cells and dendritic cells form dermal perivascular hubs that drive relapse in allergic dermatitis
papers.summary: Tissue-resident memory T (TRM) cells are heterogeneous, but how pathogenic subsets drive relapse in allergic dermatitis remains unclear. Asahina et al. identify a pathogenic CXCR6+ CD4+ TRM subset sustained through CXCL16-dependent clustering with CD301b+ cDC2s, revealing the TRM-DC niche as a potential therapeutic target for allergic dermatitis.

papers.title: Lymphatic constraint of germinal centers optimizes protective antibody responses
papers.summary: Lymphatic vessel networks remodel during infection to regulate antigen and immune cell dynamics, yet whether these changes impact humoral immunity remains unknown. Mudianto et al. demonstrate that lymph node lymphangiogenesis encapsulates activating germinal centers to constrain their size, which enhances clonal selection and protective antibody responses, establishing lymphatic vessels as structural determinants of germinal center fitness.

papers.title: Single-cell analyses of global cohorts outline determinants of immune aging and link the ratio of GZMK+ to GZMB+ Tem cells to health trajectories
papers.summary: Terekhova et al. assemble a single-cell PBMC atlas of 8 datasets, 2,609 individuals, and over 12 million cells to dissect variable and conserved features of human immune aging. CD8+ Tem GZMK+ to GZMB+ ratio distinguishes healthy from disease-associated trajectories and predicts mortality risk. This work provides a clinically relevant marker for monitoring human aging.

papers.title: Microglia-mediated extracellular matrix disruption drives neuronal dysfunction, motor impairments, and sedation following alcohol abuse
papers.summary: Alcohol’s brain effects are attributed to neurons, leaving microglial functional involvement untested. Paouri, Stanko, et al. show that microglia drive alcohol-induced sedation, motor impairment, and synaptic and neuronal loss through MyD88-dependent perisynaptic extracellular matrix (ECM) disruption. Equivalent neuron-targeted sedation bypassing microglia spares the ECM. Brain ECM loss also marks human alcohol use disorder, identifying a therapeutic target distinct from neuronal interventions.

papers.title: Glucose-deprived tumor microenvironment activates AMP-activated protein kinase to drive adoptively transferred T helper 9 cell senescence
papers.summary: Glucose deprivation in the solid tumor microenvironment impairs T cell persistence, but the mechanisms remain unclear. Fu et al. identified an AMPK-ZAK-NIK axis activated by glucose deprivation in Th9 cells that inhibits IL-9 secretion, triggering cell senescence and impaired persistence. ZAK targeting rejuvenates Th9 cells, consequently boosting the anti-tumor potency of CAR-Th9-based therapies for solid tumors.

papers.title: Aire is a cell-intrinsic regulator of natural IgM-secreting cells
papers.summary: The autoimmune regulator (Aire) promotes T cell tolerance through promiscuous gene expression in medullary thymic epithelial cells, but growing evidence suggests that it has functions beyond its canonical role in thymic tolerance. Sayed et al. demonstrate that Aire acts as a cell-intrinsic regulator of T-independent natural IgM-secreting cells, homeostatically restraining their number and natural IgM abundance.

papers.title: Microglia with distinct origins and non-canonical phenotypes coexist within the border-like niche of the brain’s circumventricular organs
papers.summary: Circumventricular organs are specialized brain regions lacking a blood-brain barrier. Van Hove et al. reveal that these regions harbor unique microglia and border-associated macrophage populations that respond to ageing and metabolism and are partly derived from fetal monocytes entering during a perinatal window, which can fully adopt the microglia identity.

papers.title: Targeting a site of vulnerability on circumsporozoite protein inhibits Plasmodium vivax malaria infection
papers.summary: Limited knowledge of protective B cell epitopes on the Plasmodium vivax circumsporozoite protein (PvCSP) remains a roadblock to vaccine development. Visweswaran et al. identify an inhibitory vaccine epitope on PvCSP that elicits antibodies capable of blocking sporozoite invasion of host hepatocytes. Definition of the structural basis for epitope recognition by a neutralizing antibody provides a roadmap for vaccine design.

papers.title: Germinal center interleukin-4 microniches drive tissue divergence of IgE memory B cell responses
papers.summary: IgE recall responses sustain allergic disease, but their anatomical regulation remains poorly understood. Villazala-Merino et al. identify Tfh cell-derived IL-4 microniches within germinal centers as an anatomical checkpoint that favors IgE recall responses in lymphoid organs while limiting their generation in the lung mucosa.

papers.title: Sensory neuronal mTORC1 kinase signaling establishes neuroimmune memory that initiates allergic immunity
papers.summary: How cumulative environmental allergen exposures are encoded by peripheral sensory neurons to shape immune responsiveness is unclear. Zhu et al. show that protease allergens induce an mTORC1-dependent, metabolically trained state in sensory neurons that amplifies later neuroimmune responses to allergens and enables cross-sensitization to antigenically distinct allergens.

papers.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is experiencing a major outbreak of Ebola disease caused by Orthoebolavirus bundibugyoense (Bundibugyo virus), which was declared on May 15, 2026. To investigate the timing of emergence and early transmission, we generated near full-length Bundibugyo virus genomes from 686 PCR-confirmed individuals across 22 health zones. We estimated the time of emergence as late February 2026 (95% highest posterior density interval [HPDI]: January 21-March 25, 2026) and an evolutionary rate of 8.7x10-4 substitutions per site per year (95% HPDI: 7.6-9.9x10-4), with no evidence of mutations associated with rapidly growing lineages.

papers.title: Drugging the immune system: principles of immunopharmacology
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Immunology, Published online: 28 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41577-026-01361-8 Immune-based therapies have transformed the treatment of cancer and inflammatory and autoimmune diseases, but treatment is often suboptimal and the ability to predictably harness the immune system for new therapies remains limited. Here, I outline four principles of ‘immunopharmacology’ that provide a framework for understanding how the immune system responds to therapeutic perturbation. These principles may help to better define how immune-based therapies work and identify new opportunities for drugging the immune system.

papers.title: How bacterial immune systems sense phage infection
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Microbiology, Published online: 02 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41579-026-01376-x Bacteria deploy diverse immune systems to counter phage infection, yet how these systems sense invasion remains incompletely understood. This Review categorizes phage-derived triggers and outlines emerging principles that govern immune recognition of phage infection.

papers.title: Microbial ecology of shallow groundwater ecosystems
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Microbiology, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41579-026-01362-3 In this Review, Karwautz and Griebler examine the microbial communities found in shallow groundwater and aquifers, exploring their diversity, functional roles and dynamic interactions with adjacent terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, as well as the influence of global change and anthropogenic pressures on these microorganisms.

papers.title: Targeting MMGT1 enhances immunotherapy efficacy in triple-negative breast cancer
papers.summary: Liu et al. demonstrate that high membrane magnesium transporter 1 (MMGT1) expression promotes immune evasion via a senescence-associated secretory phenotype that induces CD8+ T cells exhaustion. Targeting MMGT1 represents a promising strategy to improve anti-PD-1 immunotherapy efficacy.

papers.title: NKG2D overexpression potentiates CAR-T cells through costimulation by tumor NKG2D ligands
papers.summary: Li et al. show that activated CAR-T cells upregulate NKG2D ligands (NKG2DLs), rendering them susceptible to NK cells. Overexpressing NKG2D shields endogenous ligands and harnesses tumor NKG2DLs for costimulation, thereby enhancing CAR-T cell persistence, tumor infiltration, and antitumor efficacy across multiple models.

papers.title: Prediction of immunotherapy response using live tumor fragments from routine clinical biopsies
papers.summary: Predicting which patients will benefit from cancer immunotherapy remains challenging. Braun et al. use live tumor tissue from routine needle and forceps biopsies to measure ex vivo immunotherapy response. Results are consistent with clinical outcomes in a small patient cohort, including patients misclassified by current biomarker tests.

papers.title: Safety and efficacy of high-current tTIS targeting left sgACC for major depressive disorder: A randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial
papers.summary: Wang et al. demonstrate that high-current transcranial temporal interference stimulation targeting sgACC alleviates depression safely and delivers stronger short-term therapeutic effects than low-current or sham stimulation.

papers.title: Orally delivered metabolically reprogrammed probiotics for cascade-activated antitumor immunity in colorectal cancer
papers.summary: Wang et al. develop an oral metabolically engineered bacterial platform (EcN-HlpA-CGL [EHC]) for colorectal cancer immunotherapy, which triggers ferroptosis in colorectal cancer cells to boost immunogenicity, while the bacterial adjuvanticity reshapes the immunosuppressive microenvironment. This approach activates both systemic and gut mucosal immunity, effectively suppressing orthotopic tumor growth and metastasis.

papers.title: Spatially tuned localization of interleukins and OX40 agonists enhances synergistic anti-tumor immunity
papers.summary: Klich et al. use a hydrogel to deliver immunotherapy combinations intratumorally and peritumorally. Rational selection of the site of administration drives tumor clearance and long-term survivors.

papers.title: Breastfeeding and maternal microbial reservoirs are associated with infant gut phageome development during the first year of life
papers.summary: Cabello-Yeves et al. use longitudinal metagenomic analysis of mother-infant dyads to show that infant gut phageomes diversify during the first year of life and are associated with feeding-related variables and maternal microbial reservoirs. Persistent bifidophages dominate early communities, highlighting the potential relevance of phages in microbiome-targeted early-life interventions.

papers.title: Anti-HDGFL2 cryptic protein antibodies provide a sensitive readout of TDP-43 pathology and clinical disease features
papers.summary: Citrano, Maheswari Jawahar et al. develop sensitive immunoassays using second-generation polyclonal and monoclonal antibodies against HDGFL2-CE proteins and show that their levels in brain tissue associate with pTDP-43 pathology, earlier symptom onset, and shorter survival in patients with FTLD-TDP and FTLD-TDP/MND.

papers.title: AI-integrated RNA therapeutics in precision oncology
papers.summary: Symmans et al. review how artificial intelligence supports RNA therapeutic development in precision oncology, spanning multi-omics target prioritization and RNA design to delivery, patient stratification, manufacturing, and clinical translation. They distinguish clinically supported applications from preclinical and speculative approaches, outlining validation, governance, and regulatory requirements.

papers.title: Microbiota-regulated TCDCA associates with Parkinson’s disease severity and promotes BBB dysfunction through VSMC TGR5 signaling in mice
papers.summary: Zhao et al. show that circulating TCDCA associates with Parkinson’s disease severity and that TCDCA administration worsens neurovascular and motor outcomes in mice. VSMC TGR5 deletion and BSH-active L. reuteri interventions implicate a microbiota-regulated TCDCA-BBB pathway while defining its translational limitations.

papers.title: Reviving low-affinity glycan-targeting CAR with combinatorial design
papers.summary: Forcados et al. develop and test a combinatorial CAR strategy against B cell lymphoma, in which they combine CD75s and CD19 targeting. This combinatorial approach overcomes the limited efficiency of CD75s mono-targeting and lowers the risk of CAR-related toxicity seen with CD19 single targeting.

papers.title: Human genetic evidence challenges NCOA1 as a monogenic obesity gene
papers.summary: Delplanque et al. combine large-scale human genetics with functional analyses to reassess the role of NCOA1 in obesity. Despite its biological plausibility within the melanocortin pathway, pathogenic NCOA1 variants were not associated with adiposity, questioning their relevance for precision obesity therapies targeting this pathway.

papers.title: Prognostic value of cfDNA methylation in locally advanced esophageal squamous cell cancer treated with neoadjuvant immunochemoradiotherapy
papers.summary: Chen et al. track cfDNA methylation during neoadjuvant immunochemoradiotherapy for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. Methylation signals decline with treatment and are associated with pathological response and disease-free survival. The decline is reproduced in a separate 30-patient cohort, supporting further evaluation of cfDNA methylation for noninvasive monitoring.

papers.title: Microbiota-mediated naringenin release limits postoperative acute gastrointestinal injury by suppressing ferroptosis
papers.summary: Deng et al. show that reduced preoperative fecal naringenin and β-glucuronidase activity associate with postoperative acute gastrointestinal injury after cardiopulmonary bypass. Mechanistically, microbial β-glucuronidase promotes naringenin release and limits epithelial ferroptosis, highlighting candidate noninvasive biomarkers and a potential microbiota-based intervention axis.

papers.title: A spatiotemporal atlas of radiation-induced brain injury reveals dysfunction of the blood-CSF barrier
papers.summary: Quan et al. construct a spatiotemporal transcriptomic atlas of radiation-induced brain injury and show that loss of radiosensitive Tmsb4x+ choroid plexus epithelial cells triggers blood-CSF barrier dysfunction and macrophage infiltration that sustains interferon-responsive microglial activation. These findings position the blood-CSF barrier as a potential target for mitigating post-irradiation neuroinflammation.

papers.title: Lipid-engineered antibody-based therapeutics target inflamed joints and lymph nodes to enhance rheumatoid arthritis treatment
papers.summary: Zhao et al. attach multiple lipid motifs to antibody-based biologic disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (bDMARDs), enabling them to engage multiple albumin molecules in vivo and enhancing their accumulation in inflamed joints and lymph nodes. This generalizable strategy can target therapeutics larger than albumin to inflammatory sites for improved rheumatoid arthritis treatment.

papers.title: Regional brain aging signatures predict mortality through neurovascular immune mechanisms
papers.summary: Lee et al. integrate structural brain MRI with plasma proteomics to identify a three-region brain age model that predicts mortality more accurately than global measures and reveals shared immune and vascular mechanisms. These findings support regional brain aging as a scalable biomarker for precision geromedicine.

papers.title: A standardized patient-derived glioblastoma organoid platform for evaluating radiotherapy efficacy and overcoming resistance
papers.summary: Wang et al. develop a standardized reaggregated glioblastoma organoid (rGBO) platform that enables scalable evaluation of patient-specific treatment responses. The platform links organoid radiosensitivity with patient survival, identifies response-related transcriptomic signatures, and reveals BET inhibition as a strategy to enhance radiotherapy efficacy in organoid and xenograft models.

papers.title: A translational pipeline for classification of variants of uncertain significance to support gene therapy clinical trial in OTOF-related deafness
papers.summary: Chen et al. establish a translational functional pipeline to reclassify OTOF variants of uncertain significance. This pipeline enables definitive molecular diagnosis and eligibility for gene therapy trials; it further reveals that K1992R drives pathogenicity in the E1700Q haplotype via disrupting otoferlin localization.

papers.title: Oral microbial nitrate metabolism is associated with lower prevalence of prediabetes
papers.summary: Zhao et al. investigate the role of the tongue microbiome in prediabetes and glycemic dysregulation. Rothia mucilaginosa and microbial nitrate metabolism are associated with lower prediabetes prevalence and improve the prediction of prediabetes progression, highlighting oral nitrate metabolism as a potential modifiable link between the oral microbiome and metabolic health.

papers.title: Fusion-loop-engineered Zika mRNA vaccine elicits convergent B cell immunodominance to uncouple protection from ADE in macaques
papers.summary: Yang et al. demonstrate, in primates, that a fusion-loop-engineered Zika mRNA vaccine confers full protection with negligible dengue ADE. The response is dominated by convergent B cells orthologous to human IGHV5-10-1 whose antibodies target a distinct viral hotspot, with DENV envelope N67-linked glycan preventing cross-reactivity for safer flavivirus vaccines.

papers.title: Disruption of the Nav1.8/Ankyrin-3 interaction in nociceptors reduces pathological pain-like behaviors in mice
papers.summary: Chronic pain is a complex neurobiological problem whose solution is elusive. Powell et al. describe an approach to reduce chronic neuropathic pain in rodent models using a short lipidated peptide designed to inhibit the interaction between Nav1.8 and Ankyrin-3.

papers.title: Bridging innate and adaptive immunity: A bispecific SIRPαD1-αPCSK9 fusion protein reprograms macrophages for durable tumor clearance
papers.summary: Xu et al. show that blocking the CD47-SIRPα phagocytic checkpoint paradoxically elevates tumor-derived PCSK9, which degrades MHC-I on macrophages and impairs antigen cross-presentation to CD8+ T cells. A bispecific fusion protein co-targeting CD47 and PCSK9 overcomes this resistance, restoring T cell priming and achieving tumor control with improved safety.

papers.title: From patient cells to patient therapy: Twenty years of iPSC-based translation in neurodegenerative disease
papers.summary: Cha and Kim review two decades of iPSC-based translation in neurodegenerative disease, highlighting disease-specific therapeutic logic and the emerging importance of transplantation biology. They propose a phase-resolved framework for the post-transplant “biological black box” linking graft survival, maturation, host interactions, and long-term therapeutic outcome.

papers.title: Multi-omics-driven personalized management of advanced HCC
papers.summary: Sheng et al. integrate spatial multi-omics, functional models, and clinical validation to show that fibrotic stroma suppresses epithelial cGAS-STING signaling and T cell recruitment in HCC. Their GCSS model links tumor architecture to response prediction for TACE plus immune checkpoint blockade.

papers.title: Enhanced liver regeneration via targeted mRNA delivery for partial in vivo reprogramming
papers.summary: Jo et al. show that transient OSKM induction generates two distinct liver progenitor-like cell populations with limited immune activation. Liver-targeted OSKM mRNA-LNPs induce hepatocyte dedifferentiation and enhance regeneration after acetaminophen-induced liver injury, supporting transient hepatic reprogramming as a strategy for inducing regenerative plasticity with therapeutic potential for acute injury.

papers.title: In vivo-edited CCR7+IL-7+ DCs reverse T cell exhaustion by promoting T memory stem cell differentiation
papers.summary: Fu and Ma et al. develop DVH to edit DCs into CCR7+IL-7+ DCs, which target the T-zone within TDLNs and secrete IL-7 to promote Tscm differentiation. The Tscms can self-renew and generate effector T cells under antigen stimulation continuously, thereby killing tumor cells and reducing T cell exhaustion at the source.

papers.title: EZH2-dependent phenotypic plasticity reveals TTP-associated and mTORC1 therapeutic vulnerabilities in lethal prostate cancer
papers.summary: German et al. use integrated multi-omics analysis to identify EZH2 as a central regulator of prostate cancer phenotypic plasticity. The study reveals TTP-associated pathways and adaptive PI3K/mTORC1 as mediators of response to EZH2 inhibition and demonstrates that co-targeting EZH2 and PI3K/mTORC1 is an effective strategy in aggressive prostate cancer models.

papers.title: Reversal of the neutrophil barrier for potentiating immune-engineered bacteria therapy in pancreatic cancer
papers.summary: Guan et al. develop an IAA-assisted engineered bacterial therapy for pancreatic cancer. IAA suppresses neutrophil recruitment and synergizes with gemcitabine to eliminate neutrophils, boosting bacterial colonization and antitumor immune efficacy.

papers.title: A multi-omics analysis of advanced triple-negative breast cancer identifies predictors to chemo-immunotherapy and on-treatment dynamics
papers.summary: Van Renne, Agostinetto, et al. perform a multi-omics characterization of advanced TNBC to identify response predictors and treatment-induced dynamics during chemo-ICI. Poor outcomes are associated with fibrovascular and myeloid remodeling, highlighting coordinated resistance mechanisms, actionable therapeutic targets, and the value of microenvironment-based stratification for future ICI-based trials.

papers.title: Potently neutralizing and protective human monoclonal antibodies against the measles fusion protein trimer
papers.summary: Handal et al. isolate a panel of naturally occurring human monoclonal antibodies against the measles fusion protein that potently neutralize in vitro and inhibit viral replication in vivo, demonstrating strong clinical potential. Two antibodies bind distinct portions of the F protein simultaneously with epitopes spanning across multiple F protomers.

papers.title: Structural basis for broad orthopoxvirus neutralization by two antibodies targeting distinct L1R epitopes
papers.summary: Chen et al. identify two neutralizing antibodies, G4 and B9, targeting distinct epitopes on the mpox virus M1R protein (an L1R homolog). Despite targeting a conventional epitope, G4 overcomes Asp35-associated neutralization escape. Both antibodies protect against multiple orthopoxviruses in vitro and in vivo, supporting their potential as broad-spectrum antiviral candidates.

papers.title: Human iPSC models of myocardial infarction: From injury to repair and therapeutic discovery
papers.summary: Johnson et al. review how human induced pluripotent stem cells can model key stages of myocardial infarction, focusing on cell types involved across acute injury, repair, and remodeling. They examine current model strengths and limitations and discuss emerging applications in therapeutic discovery, patient-specific modeling, and regenerative cardiac repair.

papers.title: Punicalin targets RSV glycoprotein and fusion protein at non-overlapping sites to prevent viral escape
papers.summary: Xiong et al. identify that punicalin broadly inhibits respiratory syncytial virus subtypes and clinical isolates by targeting the viral G and F proteins at sites outside known resistance hotspots. It retains potent activity against drug-resistant virus and, when delivered by nebulization, reduces pulmonary viral burden and inflammation in infected mice.

papers.title: Multipronged enhancement of CART cell activity against ROR1 neoantigen by inhibition of H3K27 methyltransferase EZH2
papers.summary: Wang et al. report that inhibition of EZH2 and, to lesser degree, other epigenetic modifiers promotes expression of ROR1 neoantigen on malignant cells. CART cells targeting ROR1 are able to detect the neoantigen at very low concentration and, in combination with EZH2 inhibition, highly effectively eliminate the ROR1-expressing cells.

papers.title: iPSC-derived retinal organoids: Biological insights and progress toward photoreceptor replacement therapy
papers.summary: Mandai et al. review iPSC-derived photoreceptor replacement therapy, contrasting cone precursor and retinal organoid transplantations. They highlight host-dependent cone integration, gene-edited organoids for enhanced integration, and synaptic rewiring in the adult primate retina, providing a framework to restore vision in patients with untreatable retinal degenerations.

papers.title: Functional O-specific polysaccharide-specific antibody responses in young children following Shigella infection in Bangladesh
papers.summary: Bernshtein et al. show that functional antibodies correlate with milder shigellosis at any age, yet only individuals over 5 years of age mount lasting responses to the surface O-specific polysaccharide that drives Shigella uptake by phagocytes and triggers IL-1β and IL-18 release.

papers.title: Genome-wide cell-free DNA methylation profiling via TAPS for moyamoya disease diagnosis and postoperative collateral formation prediction
papers.summary: Chen et al. apply multimodal cell-free DNA (cfDNA) profiling via TET-assisted pyridine borane sequencing to moyamoya disease. They identify cfDNA methylation signatures that distinguish moyamoya disease from atherosclerotic cerebrovascular disease and predict postoperative collateral formation, supporting minimally invasive diagnosis and preoperative assessment of moyamoya disease.

papers.title: Combining pro-resolving therapy with cyclosporine A restores immune homeostasis and reduces toxicity in autoimmune bone marrow failure
papers.summary: Grazda et al. show that defective inflammation resolution persists in autoimmune bone marrow failure, despite standard-of-care cyclosporine A therapy. Combining resolvin E1 with cyclosporine A restores immune homeostasis while reducing toxicity.

papers.title: A blood-based metabolic signature for earlier detection of lung cancer
papers.summary: Irajizad et al. report a blood-based metabolite panel for earlier detection of lung cancer. The metabolite panel complements clinical risk models for lung cancer incidence and mortality. The panel provides a means for identifying ever-smoker individuals at elevated 1-year risk of lung cancer who would benefit from lung cancer screening.

papers.title: Therapeutic oligonucleotides as genetic medicines: The current state and future perspective
papers.summary: Godinho et al. provide an overview of nucleic acid therapies, a new class of programmable drugs that enable disease-modifying treatments by acting at the gene transcript level. The authors summarize key advances in chemistry and delivery and offer a perspective on the advances expected in the near future.

papers.title: Targeting RPL4 improves the therapeutic efficacy of PD-L1 blockade in liver fibrosis
papers.summary: Zhang et al. identify a key profibrotic function of FBXL6 in hepatic stellate cells through activation of the RPL4-YY1-PD-L1-PI3K-AKT-mTOR axis. Targeting RPL4 in combination with PD-L1 blockade achieves near-complete resolution of liver fibrosis.

papers.title: Early diagnosis and molecular classification of gastric cancer peritoneal metastasis by deep learning-driven single-cell lipidomics
papers.summary: Pan et al. combine single-cell lipidomics and graph deep learning to identify occult peritoneal metastasis in gastric cancer. The label-free platform detects rare free cancer cells, supports molecular stratification, and delivers patient-level diagnostic results within 30 min.

papers.title: Characterization of circulating neoantigen-specific T cell responses and public T cell receptors shaping immune memory in Lynch syndrome carriers
papers.summary: Duzagac et al. show that circulating tissue-surveillance neoantigen-specific T cells are detectable in Lynch syndrome carriers, even before cancer onset. Their metabolic states differ by disease stage, separating cancer-free carriers from survivors. Public TCRs spanning blood and tumor tissue open a non-invasive window for immunoprevention in mismatch repair-deficient cancers.

papers.title: Class visualizations and activation atlases for computational pathology
papers.summary: Gustav et al. introduce a concept-level explainability framework that exposes the morphology encoded by a pathology foundation model. The approach reveals prototypical histopathological features and maps the organization and overlap of tissue and cancer concepts, demonstrating that internal model representations reflect both task complexity and pathologist ambiguity.

papers.title: Iambic CEO on taking an AI drug company public
papers.summary: Fresh off a $150 million IPO, Tom Miller spoke to BioPharma Dive about the roadshow process and how he sees AI’s role in drug development evolving.

papers.title: This week in charts: Moderna’s massive stock run
papers.summary: The latest installment in BioPharma Dive’s data visualization-focused series includes a look at Moderna’s meteoric rise in 2026 and a sudden deal surge from Roche.

papers.title: Next-gen RNAi drugmaker City prices $200M IPO
papers.summary: The offering will support a trio of medicines in or nearing clinical testing, as well as earlier research into RNAi treatments that get into tissues outside the liver.

papers.title: Biogen-backed Estuary nabs $93M for kidney disease gene therapy
papers.summary: The Series A round, which was led by RA Capital, will help fund the development of two genetic medicines designed to treat an inherited kidney disorder known as "ADPKD."

papers.title: Belgian startup revives Galapagos CAR-T research
papers.summary: Armed Cell Therapeutics, chaired by former Galapagos CEO Paul Stoffels, has assumed control of cell therapies the company — now known as Lakefront Biotherapeutics — divested in a strategic overhaul.

papers.title: FDA ‘reset’ continues with new plan for reviewing rare disease drugs
papers.summary: A revamped regulatory framework may give investors less of a “guessing game” as they weigh chances for drug approvals, one analyst said.

papers.title: Iambic, an AI drug discovery specialist, banks $150M in an IPO
papers.summary: Part of a wave of young biotechs employing AI to accelerate research, the company claimed in regulatory filings that its approach has the potential to “disrupt legacy drug discovery paradigms.”

papers.title: Experimental Arrowhead RNAi drug hints at Alzheimer’s benefit
papers.summary: In a first, a subcutaneously administered RNA interference medicine crossed into the brain and plummeted levels of a protein implicated in the disease.

papers.title: Verastem cancer drug shows early promise in small study
papers.summary: Wall Street analysts believe Verastem’s drug to now be “competitive” in what’s quickly become one of the most active and crowded areas of oncology research.

papers.title: CVS to pay $315M to settle opioid prescribing allegations
papers.summary: Prosecutors say the company filled unnecessary prescriptions that fueled the opioid epidemic. A spokesperson for CVS said the company admitted to no wrongdoing and “strongly disagreed” with the case’s claims.

As Washington ramps up efforts to tighten cross-border life sciences deals involving Chinese assets, Beijing is moving to tighten its own grip on biomedical innovation, rolling out a draft policy that would ban or restrict the export of key biopharmaceutical technologies.
SimBioSys has been given FDA clearance of the Nvidia-powered TumorSight Risk, an AI and MRI-derived prognostic tool for assessing the risk of a breast cancer coming back.

Bausch + Lomb CEO Brent Saunders is making a second exit from the eye health company, as the president of parent Bausch Health steps in temporarily. Plus, Paragon Labs is buying out Apogee talent after its acquisition by AbbVie.
The FDA has issued an early alert for certain delivery systems used with Edwards Lifesciences’ SAPIEN M3 transcatheter mitral valve replacement system amid serious safety concerns.

As the world's biggest biotech hub, funding for early-stage startups has long been the lifeblood of Boston's life sciences industry. But the latest figures make for concerning reading—with average seed funding secured by a preclinical start-up plunging 40% over the past year.
Labcorp has launched the Thrive 5 Health Test that is now offered through a collaboration with Arianna Huffington's behavior change technology company, Thrive Global.
The Fierce Biotech Fundraising Tracker records venture capital rounds of $50 million or more secured by biotechs.
Estuary Biotherapeutics has swum out of stealth with $103 million in funding to power a pair of gene therapies into clinical trials for an inherited kidney disorder.
City Therapeutics has gone public with an upsized $200 million IPO, on the same day that Frazier Life Sciences listed its second biotech-focused shell company.
OrbiMed has raised $3 billion to place a fresh round of bets on biotechs and life sciences companies in the U.S., Europe and Asia.
Osivax has been forced to narrow the strategy for its influenza vaccine after the shot failed a phase 2b study.
AstraZeneca is paying insitro $40 million upfront to find novel drug targets for liver and heart diseases using artificial intelligence.
Lakefront Biotherapeutics—the new name for Belgium’s Galapagos Therapeutics—has found a buyer for its unwanted cell therapy pipeline.
Iambic Therapeutics’ IPO came in dead on target, bringing in $150 million for the AI biotech to fuel the clinical development of its oncology pipeline.
A phase 3 trial of Vanda Pharmaceuticals’ social anxiety disorder drug candidate has missed its primary endpoint, prompting the company to put the program on hold.
When Fierce last caught up with OMass Therapeutics’ CEO Ros Deegan, it was hard not to be impressed by the company’s ambition.
Clinical research giant IQVIA and cloud system provider Veeva Systems have expanded their partnership to further increase trial speed and efficiency.
iOnctura’s PI3K delta inhibitor shows promise in phase 1 study in patients with mostly pre-treated metastatic melanoma.
Verastem Oncology's decision to refocus its R&D efforts on its KRAS inhibitor appears to be paying off, at least based on initial data from a phase 1/2 trial.
Verdiva Bio has scrapped a phase 2 trial of its once-weekly oral GLP-1 drug candidate VRB-101, pulling the plug the year after launching with $410 million.

Biomea Fusion has shared phase 1 data on its oral GLP-1 prospect, shedding light on a small molecule designed to balance efficacy and gastrointestinal tolerability. Management hailed the data as a launchpad for talks with potential partners, but investors drove down the share price of the cash-strapped biotech.
Looking to expand its oncology portfolio, Gilead has tapped Vir Biotechnology’s masked T-cell engager tech in a potential $1.9 billion biobucks deal.
Up to 1,217 GSK employees in Belgium are at risk of losing their jobs as the Big Pharma rolls out its global cost-saving plans.

Zealand Pharma is paying Generate Biomedicines $30 million upfront to collaborate on multispecific drug candidates for metabolic diseases. Milestones could bring the total value of the deal above $1 billion.

Agilent Technologies is buying up the digital pathology software company Proscia in an all-cash transaction valued at $240 million with an additional $30 million on the cards for future performance milestones.

papers.summary: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01310-z Cao et al. present AMIFound, a foundation model that unifies medical image restoration across seven imaging modalities, delivering robust enhancement across diverse degradations and preserving clinically relevant information for diagnosis.

papers.title: Emotional optimization by newsroom AI needs behavioural evaluation
papers.summary: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01315-8 When newsroom artificial intelligence (AI) engages in emotional packaging, it changes how a story feels, shaping whether people approach, trust and share it. As these systems are designed and deployed, AI and behavioural researchers should work together to test whether emotional packaging helps accurate information reach readers, and whether it deepens division.

papers.title: Characterizing the role of reasoning tokens in large language models as state over tokens
papers.summary: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01303-y When large language models ‘reason’ about a problem, they might still solve it differently from what their reasoning transcript suggest. In this Perspective, Levy et al. describe how one can start investigating the role of these reasoning tokens.

papers.title: Shifting from knowledge retrieval to evidence exploration and synthesis
papers.summary: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01313-w Biomedical discovery has entered an era in which the limiting resource is no longer data, but our ability to integrate and interpret evidence. DeepEvidence, a new deep research agent, goes beyond retrieving facts and constructs explicit representations of scientific evidence.

papers.title: Large language models discover complementary heuristics for combinatorial optimization
papers.summary: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01307-8 Huatian Gong and colleagues developed LACE, a large language model-based framework that designs optimization algorithms. It builds a verified problem contract, then evolves a portfolio of complementary heuristics that together solve problems that no single method can handle.

papers.title: Towards foundation-style models for energy-frontier heterogeneous neutrino detectors via self-supervised pretraining
papers.summary: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01309-6 Alonso-Monsalve et al. demonstrate that self-supervised pretraining helps deep learning models to interpret complex neutrino detector events, improving classification, reconstruction and data efficiency while enabling transfer across different neutrino detector technologies.

papers.title: Regional climate risk assessment from climate models using probabilistic machine learning
papers.summary: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 28 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01308-7 A generative AI framework called GenFocal is introduced for climate downscaling, producing realistic fine-scale weather from coarse projections and improving regional risk estimates of compound extremes such as heatwaves and tropical cyclones.

This perspective contextualizes mathematical models by key translational challenges in CAR T therapy and identifies emerging opportunities—such as machine learning, multiscale modeling, control theory, and alternative cell types—in model-guided design of next-generation cell therapies.

FLIGHTED is applied to selection assays and to a high-throughput base-editing assay, and it improves performance of protein fitness models.

papers.summary: Long et al. integrate single-cell transcriptomes across human embryo development to construct a reference and apply complementary metrics to evaluate four blastoid protocols. Alternative NLSs rescue protein localization and expression, revealing mislocalization as a key factor in CRISPR inefficiencies in postmitotic cells.

papers.title: The drifting biochemical basis of an essential molecular interaction

papers.title: Discovery of a Novel High-Salt-Adapted Archaeal AP Endonuclease using Microfluidics-Based Cell-Free Functional Metagenomics
papers.summary: We report the discovery of a novel archaeal AP endonuclease recovered from a metagenomic library constructed from environmental DNA collected in a salt marsh ecosystem. The recovered enzyme exhibits sequence and structural homology to human APE1 and displays overlapping substrate specificity toward AP sites. The enzyme is salt adapted and retains robust catalytic activity at NaCl concentrations up to 0.5 M, a property not observed in its human homolog (APE1), consistent with adaptation to its native high salinity environment. papers.title: Generative design of functional disordered regions in a developmental transcription factor
papers.summary: Rapid advances in protein structure design have not translated to intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs). This is largely due to our incomplete understanding of how IDR sequence encodes function. Here, we use stem cell differentiation as a model to map functional sequence features in the IDR of transcription factor RUNX2. We show that RUNX2 requires its C-terminal IDR to bind chromatin and regulate gene expression during osteogenesis. Surprisingly, linear IDR sequence is dispensable, and instead features of the conformational ensemble predict function. We develop an algorithm for rational IDR design based on biophysical principles, and use it to generate functional IDRs de novo. Together, these results illustrate the central role for TF IDRs in chromatin binding and extend generative protein design beyond the folded proteome.

papers.summary: Chemokines orchestrate the migration of immune cells throughout the body, but harnessing chemokine signaling to engineer targeted cell trafficking is challenging because of their overlapping interactions and broad expression patterns. Here we used structure-guided protein design to engineer orthogonal chemokine-receptor pairs with minimal crosstalk to native systems. T cells engineered with an ortho-receptor selectively infiltrated tissues producing the ortho-chemokine, in vitro and in vivo. By engineering T cells that both sense and secrete the ortho-chemokine, we generated collective swarming behavior in which pioneer cells attract follower cells via an ortho-chemokine gradient self-organized by positive feedback. By providing orthogonal genetic control over both the generation and sensing of chemokine gradients, this system enables the construction of autonomous spatial targeting programs in engineered cells.

papers.summary: Bacterial conjugation and CRISPR base editing offer complementary routes for programmable DNA transfer and heritable genomic writing, but their combined potential for information encoding in living cells remains unexplored. Here, we introduce CONCORD, a bacterial encoding platform that couples multiplexed bacterial conjugation to genomic base editing for synthesis-free in vivo DNA data writing. A recipient Writer strain expresses the base-editing machinery and is equipped with a writing template, whereas reusable donor Guide strains deliver the encoding sgRNA signals by conjugation. Using this setup, we encode binary information into genomic DNA in a high-throughput manner. Moreover, we systematically evaluated multiple orthogonal base editors for an expanded encoding repertoire and improved data recovery through redundancy encoding. papers.title: Sense-and-response to intracellular signaling via nucleocytoplasmic localization control of a synthetic transcription factor platform
papers.summary: Many therapeutically relevant signaling pathways are sensed inside the cell, yet a modular synthetic biology platform for responding to intracellular signaling at the post-translational level is lacking. Signaling pathways control the nuclear localization and activity of native transcription factors via phosphorylation of nuclear localization/export or cytoplasmic anchor sequences. Here, we apply this concept to develop a platform of nucleocytoplasmic localization tags (NCtags) that control the nuclear translocation of a synthetic transcription factor (synTF) for transgene induction in engineered cells. We identify human-based synTF components that are basally cytoplasmic and induce transgenes under the control of NCtags with minimal background. papers.title: Directed evolution of a thermostable family-A DNA polymerase into a reverse transcriptase for 2'-modified RNA
papers.summary: RNA-based therapeutics increasingly rely on nuclease-resistant xeno-nucleic acids (XNAs), but engineering polymerases capable of reading and amplifying these non-canonical substrates remains a major challenge. Natural DNA polymerases cannot process C2' sugar modifications, and the complete structural determinants governing this limitation remain poorly understood, limiting rational design strategies. In this study, we apply directed evolution methods to Thermus thermophilus DNA polymerase using a microfluidic implementation of the Compartmentalized Self-Replication (CSR). We identify an engineered variant, termed E5, capable of reverse transcribing C2'-modified RNA, a previously inaccessible activity for this enzyme. Next-generation sequencing allow us to track evolutionary trajectories across nine rounds of evolution. papers.title: VesiScope: A stand-alone tool for the automatic detection, quantification and size analysis of GUVs from phase contrast microscopy images
papers.summary: Fluorescence microscopy is routinely used in the quantitative analysis of Giant Unilamellar Vesicles (GUVs) because it makes GUVs visible and easy to detect. Nonetheless, it requires fluorescence-equipped microscopes and, especially, the addition of tagged molecules that may introduce undesired and unaccounted variations compared to the pristine formulation. Alternatively, phase-contrast microscopy can be used to observe GUVs without labelling, yet the automatic detection of GUVs in phase-contrast images by standard image processing techniques is difficult. To overcome this limitation, we developed a framework for the automated detection and size characterization of label-free GUVs based on YOLOv11 model, a state-of-art lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for object detection. papers.title: Certified Design Regions under Parametric Plant Uncertainty with Application to Antithetic Integral Feedback
papers.summary: Kinetic parameters in engineered biomolecular circuits are typically known only within intervals and are not precisely tunable; controller synthesis is therefore naturally posed over sets of gains rather than at a single nominal design. We formulate robust controller tuning under parametric plant uncertainty as a universally quantified set-inversion problem: given a plant-parameter box, compute the controller gains that stabilize every plant in the box. Robust stability is decided by Hurwitz sign conditions, which are bounded over the joint gain-parameter domain using validated range enclosures, yielding machine-checkable certificates of local exponential stability of the deterministic equilibrium.
