papers.title: Releasing Protein Cargo from Synthetic Cells by Coupling Cell-Free Expression to Osmotic Actuation
papers.summary: Macromolecular release from synthetic cells often relies on membrane pores or channels. We explored whether internally generated osmotic stress could increase membrane permeability and promote release. Using double-emulsion microfluidics, we encapsulated an Escherichia coli cell-free expression system in Pluronic L121 polymersomes to co-express the fluorescent protein mScarlet3 and the dextranase PsDex1711 in the presence of dextran. PsDex1711-mediated dextran hydrolysis produced a greater increase in bulk osmolality than reactions without PsDex1711 DNA. Tracking hundreds of individual polymersomes showed that PsDex1711-containing populations expanded, whereas control populations contracted. The distribution of normalized fluorescence revealed a subset with lower residual fluorescence than the main population. papers.title: SynBioCrow: provenance-preserving integration of complementary retrosynthesis engines for biosynthetic pathway design
papers.summary: Motivation: Retrobiosynthesis tools use different reaction rules, search strategies and biochemical priors, so each can recover transformations missed by others. Integrating their outputs could broaden pathway coverage, but ensembling can also worsen ranking. Results: SynBioCrow runs independent retrosynthesis engines, normalizes predictions into a provenance-preserving reaction graph, and separates route generation from biochemical evidence, sequence design and bounded learning. papers.title: PepRePs: Peptide-Retargeted Phosphatases Designed with Generative Language Models
papers.summary: Phosphorylation is a fast, reversible layer of post-translational control that directly governs protein activity, signaling flux, and cell state. Kinases and phosphatases collectively establish these phosphorylation states, but their dysregulation drives cancer, neurodegenerative diseases, and developmental disorders. Selectively manipulating the phosphorylation of individual proteins in cells remains challenging, particularly for disordered substrates. Here, we introduce Peptide-Retargeted Phosphatases (PepRePs), a genetically encoded system that fuses a peptide binder to a serine/threonine phosphatase subunit to localize phosphatase activity to a target protein. We first establish the PepReP architecture using characterized tau-binding peptides, then apply protein language model-guided peptide design to target Rab8A, PTEN, and STAT3. papers.title: Targeted tumor desialylation by engineered probiotic reprograms the tumor microenvironment to potentiate immunotherapy
papers.summary: Tumor hypersialylation drives immunosuppression and limits immunotherapy efficacy by shielding tumor cells and engaging inhibitory immune receptors. Here, we engineered Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN{Delta}pgi-SAS) as a metabolically confined "desialylation catalyst" to remodel the tumor microenvironment. This strain combines HER2-directed adhesion, hypoxia-inducible surface sialidase display for targeted glycan cleavage, and sialic acid catabolism to prevent glycolytic recycling. Critically, disrupting glucose metabolism ({Delta}pgi) restricts bacterial proliferation to sialic acid-rich tumor microenvironment, significantly enhancing biosafety. In mice, EcN{Delta}pgi-SAS colonized tumors and effectively desialylated tumor cells, synergizing with anti-PD-L1 to suppress growth of immunologically "cold" tumors. papers.title: The p53-Mdm2 interaction through the lens of antithetic feedback
papers.summary: We show that the p53-Mdm2 gene interaction can be understood as a form of antithetic feedback, but with mixed feedback loops. In particular, we show that this viewpoint sheds light on the emergence and robustness properties of p53's oscillatory behaviour, as observed experimentally.

papers.title: Biotin-operated ligand trapping enables dynamic spatial redistribution of protein and organelle in living cells
papers.summary: Controlling protein localization through chemical biology tools is essential for mechanistic interrogations, functional perturbations, and therapeutic development. While existing tools cover a wide range of applications, no single approach simultaneously enables inducible trapping, controlled release, and visualization of a protein of interest (POI). To address this gap, we developed Biotin-Operated Ligand Trapping (BOLT), which combines a HaloTag-fused POI with a streptavidin trap. Desthiobiotin-conjugated Janelia Fluor HaloTag ligands enable POI visualization, trapping, and biotin-operated release. We demonstrate BOLT's capacity in synchronized secretory cargo release, microtubule-directed organelle movement and hitchhiking, and ectopically localizing nuclear transcription factor. papers.title: Design-Evolution Synergy Enables New-to-Nature Enzyme Chemistry
papers.summary: Directed evolution and machine-learning-assisted evolution have transformed biocatalysis by enabling rapid optimisation of catalytic performance within compatible protein scaffolds. In parallel, advances in deep-learning-driven de novo protein design have expanded accessible protein architectural space, enabling the generation of functional catalysts for increasingly challenging transformations. We herein report a synergistic design-evolution strategy to encode new-to-nature regio- and enantioselective C-H amination reactions using engineered de novo haemproteins to synthesise chiral piperidines, a privileged pharmacophore in drug discovery. By integrating motif scaffolding, computational re-design, and directed evolution, we demonstrate de novo enzyme design can enable challenging, high-energy-barrier enzyme chemistry with programmable regio- and enantioselectivity, high catalytic efficiency, excellent enzyme stability, and scaffold diversity.

papers.title: Designing enzymes for new-to-nature chemistry and non-natural substrates with AlphaProtein Novo
papers.summary: Creating highly active enzymes for arbitrary reactions is a transformative goal for the molecular sciences (1). Traditional protein engineering (2,3) is constrained by a reliance on existing natural starting points, which are often challenging to discover. De novo design offers the potential to overcome this by creating enzymes from first principles (4), but has yet to achieve practically relevant catalytic properties. Here we present AlphaProtein Novo (AP Novo), a machine-learning pipeline that demonstrates, for the first time, that de novo enzyme design can outperform natural sequence mining in addressing challenging chemistry. We used AP Novo to design new-to-nature nitrene transferases to synthesise the pharmacophore piperidine with unprecedented product selectivity, and to create enzymes that degrade the environmental toxin DEHP under conditions that denature natural enzymes. papers.title: Single Staphylococcus aureus SauUSI restriction enzyme motors fragment methylated DNA
papers.summary: Nature Chemical Biology, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41589-026-02353-4 Using single-molecule physics and biochemical assays, Shaw, Hughes-Games and Torres Montaguth et al. reveal how the bacterial defense enzyme SauUSI repeatedly scans and makes multiple DNA breaks, efficiently fragmenting invading genetic material.

papers.title: PRADA enables in vivo peroxidase proximity labeling for multiomics
papers.summary: Nature Chemical Biology, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41589-026-02351-6 Peroxidase-based proximity labeling has offered key insights into the molecular organization of cells in vitro, but the requirement for cytotoxic H2O2 precludes in vivo application. We engineered an enzyme fusion, PRADA, which allows peroxidase activation by non-toxic substrates, enabling spatially resolved proteomics, transcriptomics and RNA structure analysis inside living organisms.

papers.title: Targeting ribosome biogenesis
papers.summary: Nature Chemical Biology, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41589-026-02344-5 New work reveals a small-molecule inhibitor of the human ribosome biogenesis AAA-ATPase NVL that shows high selectivity and anti-proliferative activity. This holds promises for the development of better cancer drugs that target ribosome biogenesis.

papers.title: A selective NVL inhibitor suppresses tumor growth by targeting ribosome biogenesis
papers.summary: Nature Chemical Biology, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41589-026-02324-9 Guo, Tao and Cruz et al. identified a selective inhibitor named MM17 of nuclear valosin-containing protein-like (NVL), an AAA+ ATPase responsible for assembly of large ribosome subunit (60S). A bioavailable derivative, MM927, blocks 60S biogenesis, activates p53 and suppresses tumor growth, suggesting NVL as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: An RNA mark for pluripotency
papers.summary: Nature Chemical Biology, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41589-026-02337-4 A chemical modification of 7SK RNA links RNA modification to chromatin remodeling during human cell reprogramming. PUS7 installs this modification, enabling reprogramming without exogenous OCT4 and providing an alternative route to induced pluripotency.

papers.title: PUS7 pseudouridylation of 7SK orchestrates human somatic cell reprogramming into iPS cells
papers.summary: Nature Chemical Biology, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41589-026-02339-2 PUS7 promotes pluripotency through modification of the noncoding RNA, 7SK, enhancing its interaction with the BRG/BRM-associated factor complex. Replacing exogenous OCT4 with PUS7 generates induced pluripotent stem cells with more faithful epigenetic patterns and stronger developmental potential.

papers.title: The MODNAP benchmark set for modeling ribose-based modified nucleic acid and nucleic acid–protein complexes: a case study with AlphaFold 3
papers.summary: Abstract Modified nucleic acids play important roles in biology and biotechnology. However, their chemical and structural diversity as well as effects on nucleic acid structure and intermolecular interactions remain incompletely characterized. The performance of structure prediction and co-folding algorithms for modeling modified nucleic acids and nucleic acid–protein complexes has also not been evaluated. Here, we systematically analyze ribose-based modified nucleotides present in structures deposited in the Protein Data Bank. Modified nucleotides are primarily localized to the nucleobase, where they exhibit chemical and structural diversity shaped by molecular size, topological shape descriptors, and polarity-related properties. We develop MODNAP, the first curated dataset of experimentally determined structures containing modified nucleotides. papers.title: Chemically stabilized long antisense oligonucleotides perturb RNA exosome function
papers.summary: Abstract The interaction with intracellular proteins shapes the pharmacology and toxicity of RNA drugs like gapmers and siRNAs. Here, we identify the RNA exosome as a modification-sensitive interaction partner of long, chemically stabilized, single-stranded RNA drugs. Using proximity biotinylation proteomics, we observe preferential binding of the catalytic exosome subunits DIS3 and EXOSC10 to oligonucleotides stabilized by 2′-ribose modifications and phosphorothioate linkages. RNA drug binding correlates with exosome impairment as measured by dose-dependent stabilization of promoter upstream transcripts and accumulation of ribosomal RNA processing intermediates leading to reduced cell viability. papers.title: Structural basis of assembly-dependent activation of the MAD3–MAD4 nuclease in the Pseudomonas aeruginosa MADS defense system
papers.summary: Abstract The methylation-associated defense system (MADS) is a bacterial antiphage immune system that cooperates with CRISPR–Cas systems to restrict phage infection. Within MADS, the MAD3–MAD4 module has been proposed to function as an ATPase–nuclease module related to the OLD nuclease family, but the molecular basis of its assembly and function remains unknown. Here, we combined cryo-electron microscopy, X-ray crystallography, biochemical assays, and mutagenesis to elucidate the architecture and assembly mechanism of the MAD3–MAD4 complex. We found that MAD3 and MAD4 assemble into a stable 2:2 heterotetramer. Structural and biochemical analyses revealed that MAD3 alone lacks detectable ATPase activity, whereas MAD4 is insoluble when expressed alone. papers.title: HURDLER: a cloning method to overcome length limits in designed repeat proteins
papers.summary: Abstract The number of internal repeat modules remains a major limiting factor in the construction and functional exploration of long repeat proteins. As a solution, we present High-Utility Recursive Directional Ligation for Extended Repeat proteins (HURDLER)—a modular cloning strategy combining codon optimization, seamless insertion of restriction sites, and modified recursive directional ligation. It presents a very robust technique to clone DNA for large repeat proteins, which may also contain non-repetitive parts, with high fidelity requiring a minimal number of individual cloning steps. Using HURDLER, we cloned designed armadillo repeat proteins with up to 85 internal modules, corresponding to >3700 residues. papers.title: Attribute Network-based Ranking (ANeR) identifies conserved translational fingerprints of M-phase
papers.summary: Abstract Entry into M-phase requires mRNA translation, but whether mitotic and meiotic divisions share a conserved translational programme and which newly synthesized proteins promote Cdk1 activation remain unclear. Applied to 30 datasets covering mitotic and meiotic divisions, ANeR identified a conserved M-phase translational fingerprint. Benchmarking ANeR predictions against independent mitotic datasets, together with experimental validation in Xenopus oocytes, confirmed that ANeR prioritizes proteins whose accumulation increases during both mitotic and meiotic M-phases. papers.title: RiboBA: a bias-aware probabilistic framework for robust ORF identification across diverse ribosome profiling protocols
papers.summary: Abstract By mapping ribosome-protected fragments genome-wide, ribosome profiling (Ribo-seq) has uncovered extensive translation beyond conventional coding sequences, revealing non-canonical ORFs (ncORFs) with roles in diverse biological processes. However, robust ncORF identification remains challenging when Ribo-seq datasets exhibit attenuated periodicity. Protocol-induced biases during library construction is an important contributor to this loss, yet most ORF callers do not explicitly model these distortions. Here, we present RiboBA, a bias-aware probabilistic framework for robust ORF identification from Ribo-seq data. RiboBA combines a generative module that jointly infers protocol-induced biases and codon-level ribosome occupancy with a supervised module that identifies translated ORFs and initiation sites from the bias-adjusted profiles. papers.title: A tripartite RpoS-CRP-cAMP-Cra circuit orchestrates metabolic reprogramming during stress adaptation
papers.summary: Abstract The alternative sigma factor RpoS (σ S ) governs stress adaptation in many bacterial clades, yet how it coordinates stress responses with metabolic demands remains poorly understood. Thus, by integrating RNA-seq, ChIP-seq, and physiological and molecular assays, we redefined the RpoS regulon in Escherichia coli , expanding it to 667 genes and demonstrating that metabolic genes unexpectedly predominate over stress-response targets. RpoS directly drives a massive metabolic reprogramming event: it activates glycolytic and sugar transport genes while simultaneously repressing the trichloroacetic acid cycle and oxidative phosphorylation. This metabolic pivot is finely tuned by a novel RpoS-CRP-cAMP-Cra tripartite circuit to balance energy efficiency with survival during stationary phase. papers.title: Substrate energetics in non-templated DNA synthesis by terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase
papers.summary: Abstract DNA polymerases typically use deoxyribonucleoside triphosphates (dNTPs) for DNA synthesis, yet the contribution of the γ-phosphate to catalysis remains unclear. Here, we examine the role of substrate energetics in enzyme-catalyzed polymerization using a fidelity-independent model polymerase, terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase (TdT). papers.title: Distinct ways by which Srs2 helicase and Rrp1 translocase shape Rad51–DNA interactions in fission yeast
papers.summary: Abstract Precise regulation of homologous recombination is essential for genome stability. Multiple helicases and translocases prevent toxic, unscheduled association of the Rad51 recombinase with chromatin, and their levels are frequently dysregulated in cancer. It remains unclear how anti-recombinogenic enzymes act on distinct pools of Rad51. Using Schizosaccharomyces pombe , we show that the Srs2 helicase and Rrp1 translocase may target distinct Rad51 species through recombinase substrate specificity and activity control. Genetic analyses support a model in which Srs2 may preferentially regulate Rad52-dependent Rad51 nucleofilaments associated with single-stranded DNA (ssDNA), whereas Rrp1 may preferentially regulate a distinct Rad51 population associated with double-stranded DNA. papers.title: CircACVR2A(2–4) regulates stem cell pluripotency by uncoupling CDK-activating kinase functions
papers.summary: Abstract Differentiation of stem cells is driven by tightly coordinated transcriptional programs, yet the contribution of circular RNAs (circRNAs) to lineage specification remains poorly defined. Here, we profiled circRNA and messenger RNA expression during differentiation of human embryonic stem cells into five germ layer–derived lineages. Targeted silencing of dynamically regulated circRNAs revealed that depletion of circACVR2A (2–4), but not its linear counterpart, induced rapid loss of pluripotency accompanied by neuroectoderm-biased differentiation, phenotypically and transcriptionally. papers.title: Fast, flexible gene cluster family delineation with IGUA
papers.summary: Abstract Prokaryotic genomes harbor a variety of functional elements encoded as contiguous multi-gene clusters. To identify homologous gene clusters, computational tools that account for multi-gene architectures are needed to group gene clusters into Gene Cluster Families (GCFs). However, existing GCF delineation methods do not scale well to large datasets and are often limited to certain subclasses of gene clusters. Here, we present IGUA (Iterative Gene clUster Analysis; https://github.com/zellerlab/IGUA ), a scalable, flexible GCF delineation method for genomic segments with multi-gene architectures. papers.title: ZBP1 specifically binds pre-formed Z-RNA, limiting its potential pool of nucleic acid ligands compared to ADAR1

Here, we use NMR and other biophysical and biochemical experiments to characterize the Z-DNA and Z-RNA binding properties of ZBP1’s Zα1 and Zα2 domains. papers.title: PXL: a nucleic acid-binding module of the promyelocytic leukemia protein
papers.summary: Abstract The promyelocytic leukemia protein (PML) is a stress-response factor that assembles into PML nuclear bodies, dynamic subnuclear compartments involved in tumor suppression and antiviral defense. The most abundant isoform, PML-1, has been linked to transcriptional regulation, genome stability, and antiviral responses, yet the molecular basis of these functions remains unclear and is generally attributed to proteins associated with PML nuclear bodies. Here, we report that PML-1 itself harbors a previously structurally uncharacterized nucleic acid-binding domain. The domain, termed PXL, is encoded by exon 9 of the PML gene and is unique to isoform 1. papers.title: Double-base deletions and signatures associated with platinum adducts in metastatic cancer
papers.summary: Abstract Platinum compounds preferably create intrastrand G-G adducts to halt replication in cancer cells. When successfully bypassed, resulting somatic variants end up in the genome. papers.summary: Abstract Ten-eleven translocation (TET) enzymes reverse gene silencing imposed by 5-methylcytosine (5mC) in mammalian genomes by catalyzing the stepwise oxidation of 5mC to 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC), 5-formylcytosine (5fC), and 5-carboxycytosine (5caC). 5hmC both acts as an independent epigenetic mark and promotes replication-dependent DNA demethylation by antagonizing maintenance DNA methylation. papers.title: CRISPR-mediated gap-based replacement enables site-specific DNA lesion insertion into long DNA and nucleosomes
papers.summary: Abstract Defined DNA lesions are essential substrates for dissecting DNA repair mechanisms, yet existing approaches remain limited in positional flexibility, lesion diversity, efficiency, or compatibility with long and chromatinized DNA. This design enables easy and efficient insertion of diverse DNA lesions at user-defined positions without pre-engineered nicking sites or substrate redesign. papers.title: What closed-loop insulin delivery can — and cannot — teach us
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Bioengineering, Published online: 09 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s44222-026-00497-5 Closed-loop insulin delivery is one of the great success stories of autonomous medicine. Its legacy, however, is not a universal blueprint, but the recognition that each closed-loop system must be designed around the biology, risks and lived realities of each condition.

papers.title: Anticipatory intelligence in clinical microbiology
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Bioengineering, Published online: 08 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s44222-026-00502-x Clinical microbiology needs an artificial intelligence system that predicts pathogen evolution and resistance to enable prevention. Laboratories should connect forecasts to confirmatory experiments and defined actions, then test them prospectively across time and populations, as well as govern false alarms, model updates and inequitable performance as carefully as diagnostic errors.

papers.title: Fibre-architected intelligent permeable bioelectronics
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Bioengineering, Published online: 06 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s44222-026-00500-z Fibre-architected intelligent permeable bioelectronics (FIPEB) use soft, porous and multiscale fibre networks to overcome the rigidity and impermeability of conventional bioelectronics, enabling stable interfaces with dynamic biological tissues. This Review highlights how FIPEB materials, properties and scalable fabrication strategies can advance digital health care through continuous monitoring, personalized diagnosis and closed-loop therapeutic systems.

papers.title: What it takes to commercialize a bone graft
